children: Malaysian palm oil futures climbed for a second consecutive session on Monday, supported by stronger Dalian palm olein.
The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange was up 38 ringgit, or 0.77%, at 4,967 ringgit ($1,227.33) a metric ton by the midday break.
"Strength in Dalian palm olein provided support to crude palm oil prices, keeping the market in positive territory towards the midday close," a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 0.22%, while its palm oil contract
added 1.06%. The Chicago Board of Trade is closed for a public holiday.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Oil prices extended gains as tit-for-tat strikes between the U.S. and Iran on vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz and other areas heightened concerns of a prolonged supply disruption from the Middle East. O/R
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.15% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.
